# Tissue and organ dictionary — MR properties, multi-component structure, and what a voxel really contains

**Version:** 2.2 — 2026-09-09 (verification pass: twelve priority-1 PDFs read; no RECALLED component set remains). Generated by `scripts/render_tissue_dictionary_doc.py` from `mexp/tissue_data.py`; the JSON
release is `data/tissue_dictionary.json`. Companion to charter §1.2 (tissue-level threshold), §4 Phase 0, §6.1 (ground-truth
axis) and gaps register E3. Full citations are in `bibliography.md`.

## 1. Why this dictionary is a strategic component, not a convenience

The project's central question — *how many exponential components can clinical MR data support, and how precisely* — has no
answer without a population of realistic truths. The Phase 0 threshold evaluation showed that the answer at a fixed acquisition
is decided by the **amplitude vector** (the fractions of the components) more than by the placement of the time constants, the
noise model, or whether σ is known. A single myelin-like 20/80 split is one point in that space; the body is a family of very
different points: a dominant short pool with a minor long one (muscle, liver), two comparable pools (marrow, breast), a minor
short pool (grey matter), a well-separated pair with both fractions large (prostate), and genuinely mono-exponential tissues
(myocardium, blood, CSF) that any honest method must report as K = 1.

So the dictionary does five jobs. (1) It is the **ground-truth population** the harness scores every method against — each
entry's composition is a discrete truth with its clinical functional attached (§6.2 functional recovery). (2) It defines **which
functional matters per tissue** (myelin water fraction, luminal water fraction, extracellular fraction, fat fraction, perfusion
fraction), which is what Phase 3's "estimate functionals, not spectra" is scored on. (3) It states, per tissue, **whether
multi-component estimation is even physically posed**: which pools exist, which exchange fast enough to coalesce, which are
invisible to a given echo train — so that a null result in a tissue is understood as physics rather than as a failed method.
(4) It fixes **realistic acquisitions and SNRs per organ**, since a 64-echo prostate protocol and an 8-echo cardiac protocol are
different problems. (5) It is a **release artifact**: an open, cited, machine-readable table of multi-component compositions
does not appear to exist (register E3), and the harness can publish one.

Every number carries a provenance status. As of this version the count of component values is:

| PRIMARY | SECONDARY | TERTIARY | RECALLED | THEORY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23 | 17 | 1 | 1 | 14 |


## 2. How many components are "really" there? A framework for a macroscopic voxel

A clinical voxel (1–8 mm³) of any tissue contains water in several physically distinct places, plus non-aqueous protons.
Each place is a candidate exponential component. Four filters stand between that physical count and the number a fit can
recover:

1. **Exchange.** Two pools with relaxation rates R_a, R_b and exchange rate k_ex appear as one component when
   k_ex ≫ |R_a − R_b| (fast exchange), as two when k_ex ≪ |R_a − R_b| (slow exchange), and as a broadened, shifted,
   echo-spacing-dependent pair in between. On the **T2** axis (rates 5–100 s⁻¹) many membrane-limited exchanges
   (residence times 10–500 ms) fall in the slow-to-intermediate regime, so 2–3 apparent components survive. On the **T1**
   axis (rates ≈ 1 s⁻¹) the same exchange is fast, so multi-component T1 is strongly attenuated (white matter's short-T1
   fraction is 8 % at 3 T against a myelin water fraction of 15 %). Blood is the extreme: plasma–erythrocyte exchange
   (~10 ms) is fast even on the T2 axis, so blood is one component whose T2 depends on oxygenation and echo spacing.
2. **Partial volume.** At voxel scale every entry acquires neighbours' pools: CSF for brain and cord, blood for every
   perfused organ, fat for breast, marrow and pancreas, synovial fluid for cartilage. These are real components of the
   *voxel* even when absent from the *tissue*.
3. **Visibility window.** Pools with T2 below the first echo (collagen-bound water ~1–3 ms, macromolecule-associated water
   < 5 ms, cortical-bone bound water ~0.4 ms) are absent from a CPMG train starting at 6–10 ms and present in UTE. The
   harness drops them and renormalises the fractions at evaluation time rather than pretending.
4. **Intra-pool dispersion.** Orientation (magic angle in cartilage and tendon), depth zones, pore-size distributions
   (bone), and oxygenation gradients spread a "component" into a distribution. Past a point the question "how many
   components" stops being well posed and the continuum form of charter §1.2 is the right description — which is why the
   dictionary records a functional for each tissue and not only a K.

The pattern across the table below is consistent: **4–7 physical pools → 2–3 apparent T2 components → 1–2 resolvable at
clinical SNR**, with K = 3 resolvable nowhere at clinical SNR without constraining a component. The per-tissue `theory`
block records the pools, the exchange argument, and the three counts. These counts are reasoned, not measured; they are
the hypotheses the harness is built to test, and the `n_resolvable_clinical_T2` column is what the CRLB evaluation in
`results/threshold_tissues.md` checks.

## 3. Reading the tables

Times in ms; diffusivities in µm²/ms (= 10⁻³ mm²/s); water content and lipid content as mass fractions (Woodard & White
1986 Table I, chemical composition — membrane lipid included); PDFF as the fraction of MR-visible protons that are mobile
triglyceride (what Dixon/IDEAL/MRS measure — the two fat numbers differ by construction: white matter is 18 % lipid by mass and
0 % PDFF); relative proton density with CSF = 1.
Status codes: **PRIMARY** (the paper's own table/text was read), **SECONDARY** (abstract, review table, same-author
conference abstract, or the paper through a publisher-mirrored PDF), **TERTIARY** (textbook/website tabulation),
**RECALLED** (from memory; not opened), **THEORY** (a working configuration derived from physiology, not a measurement).
Ranges are literature ranges where a page gave them, otherwise the spread across the sources named.

**What the voxel contains.** 7 physical pools: myelin water (between bilayers, ~11-16 % of WM water); intra-axonal water; extra-axonal / interstitial water; glial intracellular water; blood (CBV ~ 2-3 %); CSF partial volume at voxel scale; non-aqueous protons (lipid, protein; T2 < 100 us).

*Exchange:* Myelin water exchanges with intra/extra-axonal water on ~100-300 ms (intermediate on the T2 scale, fast on the T1 scale -> multi-component T1 is exchange-attenuated); intra- and extra-axonal water exchange slowly (~0.5-2 s) but have nearly equal T2 and coalesce; glial water is unresolved.

*Counts:* apparent T2 components 3, resolvable at clinical SNR 2 — Seven physical pools reduce to three apparent T2 components (myelin, IE, CSF) because IE-scale pools share T2 within the exchange-averaged tolerance; at clinical SNR two are resolvable, and the third (CSF) is unpinned by a 320 ms window. On the T1 axis exchange leaves only a weak short component (8 % at 3 T, rising with field). Whi97 also finds the IE peak split into two broad peaks near 80 and 150-600 ms in the most myelinated structures (posterior internal capsules 88 / 12 %, splenium 93 / 7 %) and notes that components differing by less than a factor of three cannot be separated - the resolution limit of charter section 1.2 in the primary's own words.

Sources: MacK94, Whi97, Lau07, St05, Wri08, Roo07, OP19, Lab14, Pra12, SM25.

| tensor: axial diffusivity | 1.000 | 2 | 1.9–2.6 | `SECONDARY` | Maz21 PGSE TA/soleus AD 2.32/2.64; Schlaffke AD 1.89/2.14 |
| tensor: radial diffusivity (fraction 0 = same pool, second eigenvalue) | 0.000 | 1.5 | 1.35–1.6 | `SECONDARY` | Maz21 RD 1.55/1.51; Schlaffke 1.35/1.62 |

**What the voxel contains.** 6 physical pools: myofibrillar (intra-sarcomere) water; sarcoplasmic / mitochondrial water; interstitial (endomysial) water; vascular water (~ 3-5 % blood volume); macromolecule-bound water (< 5 ms); intramuscular fat (methylene protons; variable).

*Exchange:* Intracellular sub-pools exchange on ms-tens of ms and are only separable at very high SNR (Saab99's 1000-echo, SNR 3500 data); Ara14's exchange modelling puts the intracellular residence time near 1 s and the intravascular one at 0.3-3 s, i.e. slow on the T2 scale, so the long component is vascular (not interstitial) water and the interstitial T2 (~ 37 ms) is close to the intracellular one.

*Counts:* apparent T2 components 4, resolvable at clinical SNR 2 — Saab et al. needed SNR ~3500 and 1.2 ms echoes to see four components; Araujo et al. at 3 T with 2 ms spacing see two (92 / 8 % at 32 / 159 ms); a clinical 32 x 10 ms train sees the ~30 ms intracellular pool and, at best, the ~120-160 ms vascular/extracellular one (the oedema marker). St05 Fig. 1 shows three peaks in mouse muscle at 3 T without tabulating them.

Sources: Saab99, Ara14, St05, Gold04, dB04, Maz21.

*Counts:* apparent T2 components 3, resolvable at clinical SNR 2 — At clinical TE_1 = 6-10 ms the 2 ms pool is gone; what remains is a ~25 ms / ~90 ms pair with ratio ~4 and a 15 % minor fraction — resolvable at high SNR in thick cartilage, marginal in vivo where SNR and thickness are both smaller.

**What the voxel contains.** 5 physical pools: proximal/distal tubular epithelial cell water; tubular lumen filtrate (fast-flowing free fluid); peritubular interstitium; glomerular and peritubular capillary blood (high renal blood flow; f ~ 0.1-0.2); Bowman's space filtrate.

*Exchange:* Aquaporin-rich epithelium makes lumen-cell water exchange fast (ms), so tubular fluid is largely averaged into the parenchymal T2; blood and free fluid contribute a long tail; directional tubular flow gives the medulla its diffusion anisotropy.

*Counts:* apparent T2 components 2, resolvable at clinical SNR 1 — Physiologically the most compartmentalised abdominal organ, yet fast water exchange hides it on T2; the documented multi-exponential signal is in diffusion (IVIM, with the fluid/flow component) and in rat T2 at 9.4 T. A strong test case for 'exchange-coupled' ground truth (charter §6.1).

Sources: dB04, St05, vBa17, Fil15, Tas24.

Sab17's protocol is a 3D multi-echo spin echo with 64 echoes at 25 ms spacing (TE 25-1600 ms, TR 3073 ms, 1 x 1 x 4 mm, 11 min) at an average prostate SNR of 103 (95 % CI 81-125), chosen by simulation over TE 7-55 ms and NE 10-64 for T2short 25-75 / T2long 200-800 ms; the v2 acquisition (64 x 8 ms, SNR 80) was wrong in the spacing, so the v2 'own acquisition' row of the threshold table was evaluated on a 512 ms window instead of 1600 ms. Regularised NNLS (Bjarnason & Mitchell 2010) on a 20-2000 ms grid with the short/long cut at 200 ms from the histogram of 4700 two-peak pixels; Ncomp 2.09 +/- 0.22 in nonmalignant PZ, 1.81 in malignant PZ (higher-grade tumours become mono-exponential)*

| component | fraction | value | range | status | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| epithelial / stromal water | 0.760 | 90 | 52–150 | `PRIMARY` | Sab17 Radiology Table 2, nonmalignant PZ, 18 patients: T2short (gmT2 of the 20-200 ms peak) 90 +/- 26 ms, range 52-150; JMRI Table 3 median 75 (50-152); nonmalignant TZ 104 +/- 38 |
| luminal water (fraction range 0.09-0.45; malignant PZ 0.10 +/- 0.05 at 548 +/- 188 ms) | 0.240 | 545 | 300–887 | `PRIMARY` | Sab17 Radiology Table 2: T2long (200-2000 ms peak) 545 +/- 115 ms, range 300-887, LWF 0.24 +/- 0.09 (0.09-0.45); JMRI Table 3 median 503 (249-904), LWF 0.20 (0.03-0.50); LWF vs histological luminal area rho 0.75 with slope 0.45, vs Gleason score rho -0.78 |

**What the voxel contains.** 4 physical pools: glandular lumen fluid (secretions; large in normal PZ: 27 % of the section area by histology, Sab17 JMRI); epithelial cell water; stromal (smooth muscle/fibrous) water; vascular blood.

*Exchange:* Lumen-epithelium exchange is slow relative to the large T2 difference (ratio ~ 6), so two components persist; stroma and epithelium share T2 and coalesce. Cancer replaces lumen with cells -> LWF falls (0.24 -> 0.10 in PZ). Sab17 JMRI attributes the LWF-vs-histology slope of 0.45 partly to lumen-epithelium water exchange and partly to 2D-area vs 3D-volume and fixation shrinkage.

*Counts:* apparent T2 components 2, resolvable at clinical SNR 2 — Well-separated (ratio ~ 6), both fractions large: the easy case, and the positive control for every estimator; the malignant PZ variant (LWF 0.10 at 81 / 548 ms) is the pathology-axis row for this organ.

Sources: Sab17, dB04, Boj17.

| component | fraction | value | range | status | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| adipocyte / interstitial water | 0.100 | 40 | 30–60 | `THEORY` | Woo86 water 11-31 % by mass -> ~ 8-25 % of visible protons; T2 of the water fraction of adipose tissue not reached; placed at 30-60 ms |

**What the voxel contains.** 5 physical pools: adipocyte triglyceride: methylene (CH2)n, ~ 70 % of lipid protons; other triglyceride resonances (methyl, olefinic, alpha/beta-carboxyl, glycerol, diallylic) ~ 30 % — the six-peak model; adipocyte cytoplasmic water (thin rim around the lipid droplet); interstitial / stromal water and capillary blood; collagenous septa (short T2, invisible at clinical TE).

*Exchange:* Lipid and water protons do not exchange; the lipid resonances are separated by chemical shift (up to ~ 5 ppm), not by relaxation, and their CPMG decay is modulated by J-coupling so the apparent fat T2 depends on echo spacing and refocusing quality (Hen92).

*Counts:* apparent T2 components 2, resolvable at clinical SNR 1 — A ~ 90/10 lipid/water mixture whose dominant component is not a fixed exponential: the right model is chemical-shift-encoded with a single fat T2*, and any multi-exponential T2 fit is misspecified by construction. In the harness this row tests the model-misspecification axis (charter §6.1), not K; PDFF is its functional.

Sources: Woo86, Gold04, dB04, Boj17, Hen92, Ham11.


## 5. Verification status and what moves a row

| Status | Component values | What moves it |
|---|---|---|
| PRIMARY | 23 | — (re-check only if the source is corrected) |
| SECONDARY | 17 | opening the paper's own table (PDF in `literature/`) → PRIMARY |
| TERTIARY | 1 | replacing the website/textbook number with the primary it cites |
| RECALLED | 1 | opening the named source (the one remaining value is the renal-medulla IVIM D*; no RECALLED *component set* remains as of v2.2) |
| THEORY | 14 | a multi-component relaxometry study of the organ (none reached for liver, spleen, kidney, pancreas in vivo — see §6, *future research project*) — or the harness's own simulator-plus-estimator results marking the split as unsupported; the three CSF partial-volume components of the brain and cord rows are THEORY because the primaries see the > 1 s peak but do not tabulate its voxel fraction |

Bulk properties (water/PD, T1, T2, ADC, lipid, PDFF) carry their own status per value in the tables above. As of v2.2 the
water contents and lipid mass fractions rest on Woodard & White 1986 Table I (PRIMARY) with Whittall 1997 Table 2 for brain,
the abdominal and pelvic T1/T2 columns at both fields on de Bazelaire 2004 Tables 1–2 (PRIMARY), the fat and MSK relaxation
times on Gold 2004 (PRIMARY), the marrow fat fraction on Le Ster 2016 Table 1 (PRIMARY), and every Stanisz 2005 value on
Table 1 of the publisher PDF (PRIMARY; re-read 2026-09-09, no number changed). The component sets of brain WM and GM (Whittall
1997, MacKay 1994), cervical cord (MacMillan 2011), skeletal muscle (Saab 1999, with Araujo 2014 at 3 T), WM T1 (Labadie 2014),
Achilles tendon (Du 2012) and prostate (Sabouri 2017 ×2) were moved to PRIMARY from the papers' own tables in the v2.2 pass;
Reiter 2009, Horch 2010 and Luciani 2008 had been read in full before. PDFF values for lean organs remain RECALLED ranges from
the water–fat imaging literature: none of the 57 PDFs on hand is a water–fat paper for those organs, and the papers that would
settle them are listed in `literature-requests.md` (priority 1b).

## 6. What is missing, by design of the next passes

- **Pathology as a second axis.** Every entry is the normal tissue. The clinically decisive cases are the *changes*: MS
  lesion (myelin water loss), oedematous muscle (extracellular fraction up), steatotic liver (PDFF above the 5.56 % cut-off of
  Szczepaniak 2005, graded ~ 6.4 / 17.4 / 22.1 % by Tang 2013 — a chemically shifted fat pool added to the T2 mixture) and
  iron-loaded liver (T2 collapse), fatty pancreas and fatty infiltration of muscle and myocardium (PDFF up), prostate cancer
  (luminal water fraction down — Sabouri 2017 already gives the row: malignant PZ LWF 0.10 ± 0.05 at 81 / 548 ms against 0.24 in
  nonmalignant PZ), oedematous muscle (Araujo 2014's venous-filling state is a measured surrogate: the long fraction rises from
  8 to 14 % and its T2 from 159 to 181 ms), cartilage degeneration (Reiter's trypsin-degraded row: 64/149 ms, 11/86 %),
  bone-marrow infiltration (fat fraction down), myocardial oedema and fibrosis, MS lesions (MacKay 1994: MWF 4.1–6.4 % against
  15.6 % in normal WM). The schema takes a `condition` field without change; the next dictionary revision adds one pathological
  variant per organ with its own sources, starting with steatotic liver at PDFF 10 and 25 % (charter §10 step 8e).
- **Abdominal multi-component measurements — a future research project, not current focus.** No in vivo multi-component T2
  study of liver, spleen, kidney or pancreas was reached; the splits are THEORY and say so. Measuring them (multi-echo
  relaxometry with IVIM in the same session, so that the T2 and diffusion compartment fractions can be compared) is recorded
  in the gaps register (E3) as a candidate project for later, and the dictionary will take the values when they exist.
- **Organs not yet covered:** lung (very low PD, T2* dominated), skin, placenta, bowel wall, lymph node, testis, brain tumour
  heterogeneity (a continuous-spectrum truth rather than discrete), peripheral nerve, intervertebral disc (two-pool
  nucleus/annulus), fat-water phantoms as the calibration row.
- **Field-strength completeness.** 1.5 T and 3 T are carried; 7 T (MWF rises, T1 lengthens, T2 shortens) and 0.55 T (T1
  shortens — the low-field renaissance) are the two ends the harness should also test.
- **Diffusion beyond scalar/IVIM.** The white-matter standard model and muscle/cardiac tensors are carried as
  compartment sets; the kernel that consumes them (`diffusion_standard_model`, b-tensor kernel) is exercised on the base
  class in tests but not registered (charter G2).
- **Proton density from a quantitative primary.** Water-content numbers now rest on Woodard & White 1986 (chemical
  composition, PRIMARY) with Oros-Peusquens 2019 for brain; the *relative PD* column is still a tertiary table, and Mezer 2013 /
  Volz 2012 / Abbas 2014 (quantitative MR water mapping) remain to be opened to replace it.

## 8. Dictionary changelog

- 2026-09-07 v1: 13 entries, all RECALLED (first draft).
- 2026-09-07 v2: restructured (properties: water/PD, T1, T2 at 1.5 and 3 T, ADC; components per modality; theory block); 20 entries; verified values from Stanisz 2005 (SECONDARY, table via mirror), de Bazelaire 2004 (abstract), Han/Gold 2003, Reiter 2009 (PRIMARY), Horch 2010 (PRIMARY), Saab 1999 (abstract), MacKay 1994 / Whittall 1997 (abstract/preview), Labadie 2014 (abstract), Luciani 2008 (PRIMARY table), van Baalen 2017, Filli 2015, Serafin 2024, Mayer 2021, McGill 2015, Mazzoli 2021, Oros-Peusquens 2019; liver, spleen, kidney cortex/medulla, pancreas, marrow, blood, CSF added; abdominal T2 splits are THEORY (no multi-component study reached) and say so.
- 2026-09-09 v2.1: adipose tissue added (19 entries); lipid mass fraction (Woodard & White 1986 Table I, PRIMARY) and PDFF added to every entry as two distinct quantities; Woodard & White 1986, de Bazelaire 2004 (Tables 1-2), Gold 2004 (Tables) and Le Ster 2016 (Table 1) read from the PDFs in literature/ — water contents and the abdominal/pelvic T1/T2 columns moved to PRIMARY, 1.5 T columns filled for spleen, kidney, pancreas, prostate and liver; fat T2 recorded as sequence-dependent (J-coupling) with both the T2-prep and the SSFSE values; hepatic steatosis and the other fat pathologies noted under the pathology axis (not entries yet). The abdominal multi-component T2 splits remain THEORY: measuring them is recorded as a potential future research project (register E3), not current focus.
- 2026-09-09 v2.2 (verification pass, charter section 10 step 8a): twelve priority-1 PDFs read from literature/ and applied. Prostate (Sabouri 2017 Radiology Table 2 / JMRI Table 3): the last RECALLED component set moves to PRIMARY - LWF 0.24 (not 0.35), T2short 90 / T2long 545 ms, and the protocol is 64 x 25 ms at SNR ~ 100 (not 64 x 8 ms). Brain WM / GM (Whittall 1997 Tables 1-3, MacKay 1994): MWF 0.113 / 0.031 with the Whittall structure averages, IE gmT2 77 / 80 ms; the CSF-like partial-volume components relabelled THEORY (seen but not tabulated by the primaries). Spinal cord (MacMillan 2011 Tables 1, 3, 4): MWF 0.296, IE 100 ms. Skeletal muscle (Saab 1999 Table 1): four components at 10.9 / 27.8 / 45.5 / 11.3 % (the v2 5 % for the 114 ms pool was the fifth component's share), field 1.89 T; Araujo 2014 (3 T, two components 92 / 8 % at 32 / 159 ms, exchange model) recorded in the note. WM T1 (Labadie 2014 Table 2): 0.083 at 225 ms, T1,long 1.06 s, Look-Locker geometric TIs. Tendon (Du 2012 Table 1): 71.4 % at 1.28 ms + 28.6 % at 17.65 ms (the v2 numbers were the ligament row); Du 2012 also added to cartilage and cortical bone notes; Bouhrara 2015 (Rician-correct biexponential T2*, bovine nasal cartilage) to the cartilage note; Prasloski 2012 (EPG stimulated-echo correction, simulated WM truth 15 / 75 / 10 %) to the WM note. Stanisz 2005 Table 1 re-read from the publisher PDF: every St05 value moves to PRIMARY unchanged. PDFF ranges for the lean organs stay RECALLED: none of the 57 PDFs on hand is a water-fat paper for those organs (requests added to literature-requests.md).
